video_title: Rich Paul Gets BRUTALLY Honest About Kuminga Taking LESS MONEY

quotes.speaker: Rich Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's contract negotiations and team fit
quotes.excerpt: Jonathan Kuminga turned down 100 billion dollars from the Warriors and he wound up signing a two-year 12.4 million dollar deal

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Paul
text_blocks.text: Jonathan Kuminga turned down 100 billion dollars from the Warriors and he wound up signing a two-year 12.4 million dollar deal with the T-Wolves, second year is a player option. Rich, the actual, it was he turned down 36 million from the Lakers reportedly. But what was the Warriors offer to Kuminga? It was much bigger than 12.4 million a year.

text_blocks.speaker: Jonathan Kuminga
text_blocks.text: That was last year though. That was last year. But usually, when Fat Joe said yesterday's price not today's price, Kuminga's hustling backwards.

quotes.speaker: Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.summary_phrase: How NBA players should approach contract negotiations
quotes.excerpt: When you in the contract negotiation or when you up for a negotiation, your value in that moment is a lot different
quotes.quote: As a player in the NBA or in any sport, when you in the contract negotiation or when you up for a negotiation, your value in that moment is a lot different. Now, a year later, could you increase your value? Absolutely. For a lot of guys, especially when you go high in the draft, your best chance of really having the most value is probably going to be with your host team, the team that drafted you, especially if they took you.

quotes.speaker: Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.summary_phrase: General managers and the decision to pay players
quotes.excerpt: If the general manager don't want to pay you, either you're not as good and he made a mistake
quotes.quote: Essentially, if the general manager don't want to pay you, either you're not as good and he made a mistake, or they found somebody to replace you and you're not as good.

quotes.speaker: Rich Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's role and fit on an NBA team
quotes.excerpt: Kuminga to me, ideally, is a seventh man on a great team
quotes.quote: Kuminga to me, ideally, is a seventh man on a great team, meaning if there's a playmaker against the other team's bench and Kuminga is playing with that playmaker, he will kill a tired first unit in a second unit. He'll look like a superstar there. And maybe he can fit in with the first unit in Minnesota because without a kind of traditional power forward, they can be a very athletic, scary kind of team and maybe he can fit in.

quotes.speaker: Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.summary_phrase: The reality of being a role player in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: There's 30 starring roles in the NBA, maybe 45 because some teams have two guys that can actually be stars
quotes.quote: When you come into the league, there's two ways to come into the league. You're coming into the league with an opportunity to possibly become a number one guy, or you come into the league as a role guy and that's just what you're going to be. How you embrace that is a whole other thing, because I always say there's 30 starring roles in the NBA, maybe 45 because some teams have two guys that can actually be stars. Everyone else has to play a role.

quotes.speaker: Rich Paul
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Jordan Poole's value and contract situation
quotes.excerpt: When Jordan Poole's the comp, he's going to be paid one way
quotes.quote: When Jordan Poole's the comp, he's going to be paid one way. But if you look at Maxey and go, injury's okay, age is okay, Jordan Poole is not the comp.

quotes.speaker: Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.summary_phrase: Learning from past contract negotiation mistakes
quotes.excerpt: There's been times where I probably should have pushed the player a little bit harder to take a deal
quotes.quote: There's been times where I probably should have pushed the player a little bit harder to take a deal and I didn't, and they never got back to that. That's part of it, but you learn from that.
